intent: Eight original tasks distinguish loss, debt, lend, owe, earn, donate, charity and fund with accurate participant directions and event order.
picturePurpose: Original hypothetical coat and shirt comparison identifies warm coats without inventing actual charity inventory; direction and event labels remain coded.

transfer.stem: Which account preserves the debt direction, lending direction and donation order?
transfer.passage:
Keeping directions and promises clear
The shop reported a small loss after a flood, without stating an exact amount. A family made a plan to pay off a debt. The plan did not prove repayment. I still owed you two pounds for tickets, so I was the person who needed to pay you, not the other way round.
I asked, “Could you lend me a pencil until lunch?” You would lend it and I would borrow it. My question did not prove agreement or delivery. A friend hoped to earn money by repairing bikes, but no income had yet been confirmed.
We planned to donate books after everyone had read them. Everyone needed to finish before donation; a date and recipient were not supplied. A charity provided warm coats in winter. A separate fictional picture compared a thick coat with a thin T-shirt; it was not an inventory record. A fund helped families replace flood-damaged books, without proving that every replacement had already happened.

options.text: I owe you two pounds; you lend a pencil to me; everyone reads the books before we donate them.
You owe me two pounds; you lend a pencil to me; everyone reads before donation.
I owe you two pounds; I lend my own pencil to you; everyone reads before donation.
I owe you two pounds; you lend a pencil to me; we donate before everyone finishes reading.

把所有人读完后捐倒成之前捐。
